title: No Universal Courtesy: A Cross-Linguistic, Multi-Model Study of Politeness Effects on LLMs Using the PLUM Corpus

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the Composite Quality Score (CQS) and other multidimensional response metrics of LLM outputs across English, Spanish, and Hindi to identify performance disparities, processing biases, and a persistent performance advantage favoring English.

Assessing whether LLM responses appropriately align with culturally specific politeness norms (e.g., preference for directness/assertiveness in Spanish vs. indirectness/deference in Hindi) across different politeness prompt categories, or if they disproportionately default to English-centric sociolinguistic norms.

Using the zero-shot classifier 'unitary/toxic-bert' to automatically score the presence of offensive or biased language generated in model responses across various levels of prompt politeness and impoliteness.
